description: What is new since the last time the user caught up: new workouts (date, startLocal, activityId, totalTimeS, tss, guide, workoutKey), new finished nights (bedtimeStart/End, durationS, score, avgHrv, recoveryOnWaking), new recovery samples (count, latest, low, high), the plan items (from set_plan) in the review window as done / missed / pending by DATE (any workout on a planned date counts as done: the sport and the guide are not compared), and daysSinceLastSession. Toward Suunto it only reads: list calls for workouts (pages of 50, at most 4 pages per call), sleep and recovery. The first call looks back 7 days (the list calls add a margin of up to 14 hours for time zones); later calls start at the review window's first day, which is the day every section was last read completely (never more than 14 days back; anything older is reported in notes and was not looked at), and list workouts 2 days further back so a late sync is found. 'New' means after the marker kept in ~/.suunto-mcp/seen.json (SUUNTO_SEEN_PATH overrides it): workouts by key (a workout that syncs late with an earlier start is still new, once), nights by end time, recovery by sample time. Pass markSeen: true only once the user has actually been told. markSeen false (the default) is a PURE READ: nothing is written and the same call repeats the same answer. With markSeen: true each section that was read moves its marker, and `marked` is true; the review window (sleep, recovery and plan items) moves forward only when EVERY section was read (no entry in `errors`, the plan file readable, the whole workout list read), so what a failed section missed is reported next time. If there are more workouts than one call reads, `errors` says so, the call reports what it read, and calling again with markSeen: true continues below where it stopped. Plan items are reviewed from the review window's first day, so an item can show again until the window moves. A night still being recorded and naps are not reported. Output: { today, since: { from, firstCall }, newWorkouts, newNights, recovery, plan (null without a plan, { error } if the plan file is unreadable), lastSessionDate, daysSinceLastSession, markSeen, marked, errors, notes }. An unreadable seen.json is an error and is never overwritten. In demo mode the marker is kept in memory. Annotated not read-only (and idempotent: marking twice leaves the same marker) only because markSeen: true writes that small local marker, so clients may ask for permission before running it; the call itself changes nothing at Suunto.

markSeen.description: true: move the marker to what this answer covers (do it only after telling the user). false (default): leave it, so the next call repeats this answer.

name: get_catchup
title: Catch up: what is new since last time
